answer: The Weekly community check-in streak over sixty days verified by attendance records turns patience into the price of identity: every week the applicant signs in, the attendance records go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so one real person can keep a single identity alive while a farm cannot keep hundreds. Even a quiet dawn gets heard, because attendance weighs persistence, not volume. When the ivory settles over the trellis, the streak holds because every week carried its own proof.
